Write a [SymPy](https://docs.sympy.org) equation, fill in
[Pint](https://pint.readthedocs.io/) quantities, and get the full working:
the symbolic form, the substituted form, and the result, rendered as
LaTeX in your [marimo](https://docs.marimo.io) or Jupyter notebook.

[Get started](getting-started.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[GitHub](https://github.com/bedrock-engineer/symeval){.btn .btn-outline-secondary}
[PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/symeval/){.btn .btn-outline-secondary}

```sh
pip install symeval
```

## Highlights

- ✨ **Crystal-clear**: shows the full working, that is symbolic form, substituted form, and result.
- 🐍 **Pure Python**: drop into your interactive notebooks and other Python code, no special syntax, no cell magic, no Domain-Specific Language (DSL).
- 📏 **Unit-aware**: pint quantities carry units through every step and convert to your chosen output unit.
- 🧮 **Sympy-native**: rearrange or simplify your formula symbolically first, then evaluate.
- 📊 **DataFrame-ready**: use `quantity_evalf()` to compute a new unit-aware column on a DataFrame.

## Quickstart

Define the equation, substitute quantities, and SymEval renders how the result
is reached:

```python
from pint import Quantity
from sympy import Eq, Symbol
from symeval import sym_evalf

axial_stress = Eq(Symbol(r"\sigma"), Symbol("F") / Symbol("A"))

sym_evalf(
    axial_stress,
    subs={
        Symbol("F"): Quantity(-680, "kN"), 
        Symbol("A"): Quantity(10_580, "mm^2")
    },
    output_unit="MPa",
    decimals=2,
)
```

$$\begin{align*}
\sigma &= \frac{F}{A} \\
&= \frac{\,-680\ \mathrm{kN}}{\,10580\ \mathrm{mm}^{2}} \\
\sigma &= -6.43\times 10^{7}\ \mathrm{Pa} = -64.27\ \mathrm{MPa}
\end{align*}$$

The output symbol comes from the equation, so you do not pass it separately.
Head to the [tutorial](getting-started.qmd) for the reactive walkthrough,
or read [how symeval works](explanation.qmd) for the ideas behind it.
